title: Sharp Momentum
intro: This detector measures momentum, not position, and it clicks at t = 8. The view switches to momentum space |φ(k)|²: the target is a small disc around the packet's mean momentum. A packet of width σ has a momentum spread of 1/(2σ) (σ_x·σ_k ≥ ½), so landing in a sharp momentum window takes a packet that is wide in space. But the world is only so big: its edges swallow a packet that is too wide.
goal: Set the packet's width. At t = 8 the world measures its momentum: land inside the small disc in the momentum view.

physics.point: Position and momentum cannot both be sharp. A packet narrow in space has a broad spread of momenta, so to land in a small momentum window it must be wide.

idea: A wave packet is a sum of plane waves with different wavenumbers k. A narrow bump needs many different k; a long, smooth wave train needs only a few. So the spread in position and the spread in momentum trade off. This is Heisenberg's uncertainty relation.
Here the detector measures momentum. The target is a disc of radius 0.25 around the packet's own momentum, k = (1, 0). Only a packet with a small momentum spread puts most of its probability inside.

A free particle's momentum distribution does not change in time, so waiting does not help. The limit is the world: it is 40 units wide, and its absorbing edges eat the tails of a packet that is too wide, which also spreads its momentum.
maths: A Gaussian sits exactly on the bound: if σ is the position spread of |ψ|² along an axis, the momentum spread along it is σ<sub>k</sub> = 1/(2σ).
The chance of a momentum within r = 0.25 of the centre is 1 − exp(−r²/2σ<sub>k</sub>²) = 1 − exp(−σ²/8). In an infinite world that is 12 % at σ = 1 and 96 % at σ = 5.

On the game's grid, momenta come in steps of 2π/40 ≈ 0.16, close to the target's size, so σ = 5 starts at about 90 %. By t = 8 the packet has drifted to x ≈ 28, the edges have absorbed about 5 %, and 82 % is left.
Wider is worse again: σ = 8 loses 19 % to the edges and scores 72 %; σ = 10 loses 28 % and scores 64 %.
try: Play with the default σ = 1. In the momentum view the blob is much larger than the disc, and P<sub>T</sub> ≈ 12 %. Before you press Play, the readout shows Δx·Δk<sub>x</sub> = 0.50: the packet is exactly on the bound.
Set σ = 5. The blob shrinks to fit the disc, and P<sub>T</sub> is about 82 % at t = 8.
Set σ = 10. The momentum blob is tiny, but the lost meter climbs to about 28 % by t = 8 and P<sub>T</sub> ends near 64 %.
